title: Trace energy under a constant Weil twist
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ of characteristic $p$, an algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and an isomorphism $\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$ as in [def-weil-punctual-weights]. Let $X_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme. For a constructible Weil sheaf $\mathcal H$ on $X_0$, $m\ge1$, and $y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$, write $t_{\mathcal H,m}(y)=\operatorname{Tr}(F_y^{(m)}\mid\mathcal H_{\bar y})$, with the local operator of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace], and set $S_m(\mathcal H)=\sum_{y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})}|\iota t_{\mathcal H,m}(y)|^2$.
Let $\mathcal F$ be a constructible Weil sheaf on $X_0$, let $b\in\Qlb^\times$, and let $w\in\mathbf R$ satisfy $|\iota(b)|=q^{-w/2}$. For the constant twist $\mathcal B_b$ of [def-wf-constant-weil-twist], for every $m\ge1$ one has
$$S_m(\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal B_b)=q^{-mw}S_m(\mathcal F).$$

source.place: Step 1, twist trace-energy identity; project TraceEnergy.lean:420-427, traceEnergy_constantTwist

proof.text: Write $\theta$ for the Weil isomorphism of $\mathcal F$. In [def-wf-constant-weil-twist], the geometric sheaf of $\mathcal B_b$ is the constant coefficient line, with distinguished vector $1$, and its one-step geometric Frobenius is multiplication by $b$. Under the tensor-unit identification $v\otimes c\mapsto cv$ (inverse $v\mapsto v\otimes1$), the underlying sheaf of $\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal B_b$ is therefore $\mathcal F$. The tensor Weil map of [def-wf-tensor-product] is $\theta\otimes(b\,\mathrm{id})$, hence is $b\theta$ under this identification: on a pure tensor its value is $\theta(v)\otimes bc$, which maps to $bc\theta(v)$. This unit calculation applies to a constructible sheaf without any lissity or connectedness assumption.

source.place: Step 1, constant-line twist and its Weil map

proof.text: Fix $m\ge1$ and $y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$. Use the same geometric point, point transport, and pullback-composition maps for the two sheaves, which have the same underlying sheaf by step 1. In the recurrence of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace], replacing $\theta$ by $b\theta$ replaces $\theta^{[m]}$ by $b^m\theta^{[m]}$: for $m=1$ this is step 1, and the next composite is $(b^m\theta^{[m]})\circ L(g_X^m)^*(b\theta)=b^{m+1}(\theta^{[m]}\circ L(g_X^m)^*\theta)$. Pullbacks are coefficient-linear by the rational morphism convention of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and the point-fiber functor is coefficient-linear by [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. For $\Qlb$ these computations are read at a common finite coefficient field containing $b$ and the sheaf's data, then embedded in $\Qlb$, as in those definitions. Thus the local operator becomes $b^m F_y^{(m)}$. If $A=(a_{ij})$ is its matrix on the finite-dimensional stalk of $\mathcal F$, the twisted matrix is $(b^m a_{ij})$. Summing its diagonal entries by [def-weil-endomorphism-trace] gives $t_{\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal B_b,m}(y)=b^m t_{\mathcal F,m}(y)$. The exponent is $m$ because the local operator is the $m$-fold return; no assertion that the closed-point degree of $y$ equals $m$ is used.

source.place: Step 1, pointwise trace identity, expanded at rational points

proof.text: Put $z=\iota(t_{\mathcal F,m}(y))$. Since $\iota$ preserves products, the identity of step 2 and multiplicativity of the complex absolute value give $|\iota(t_{\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal B_b,m}(y))|^2=|\iota(b)|^{2m}|z|^2$. Here $q>1$ and the assumed equality $|\iota(b)|=q^{-w/2}$ implies $|\iota(b)|^{2m}=\exp(2m(-w/2)\log q)=\exp(-mw\log q)=q^{-mw}$. Consequently each summand in the twisted energy is $q^{-mw}$ times its untwisted summand.

source.place: Step 1, squared absolute values and the normalization exponent

proof.text: The scheme $X_0$ is of finite type over $k_0$, and $\mathbf F_{q^m}/k_0$ is a finite field extension. Thus [lem-weil-point-counts-finite](1) makes $X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$ finite. Sum the equality in step 3 over this set. The factor $q^{-mw}$ is independent of $y$, so distributivity of a finite sum gives $S_m(\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal B_b)=\sum_y q^{-mw}|\iota(t_{\mathcal F,m}(y))|^2=q^{-mw}S_m(\mathcal F)$. For an empty point set both sums are zero. Since $m\ge1$ was arbitrary, this proves the statement.
